cinny.description:
Cinny, a Matrix web client: a stateless Deployment of its own, so a client patch
never restarts the homeserver.

affinity.description: Affinity, merged over the chart default: a preferred pod anti-affinity that spreads the replicas over nodes (set `podAntiAffinity` to replace it).

config.description: Cinny `config.json` (homeservers, featured communities, hash router, see `config.json` upstream), merged over the chart defaults: `homeserverList: [<serverName>]`, `defaultHomeserver: 0`, `allowCustomHomeservers: false`. Cinny resolves each entry of `homeserverList` through its `/.well-known/matrix/client`: use `ingress.wellKnown` or `httpRoute.wellKnown` when `serverName` is not the homeserver host. The browser reads the file, so keep secrets out.

enabled.description: Create a Gateway API HTTPRoute for Cinny (path prefix `/`).

hostnames.description: Host names (empty: any host of the Gateway listener).

digest.description: Image digest, only valid together with `cinny.image.tag`.

tag.description: Image tag. Empty: the tag and digest recorded for `cinny.image.repository` in the `artifacthub.io/images` annotation of `Chart.yaml`. When set, the chart digest is not applied; add `cinny.image.digest` to pin it.

hosts.description: Host names. Required when enabled. Not the homeserver host unless you route paths yourself: both Ingresses serve `/`.

minReadySeconds.description: Seconds a new pod must be ready before it counts as available (rolling updates never drop below `replicaCount`).

maxUnavailable.description: Pods that may be unavailable at once (a number or a percentage).

replicaCount.description: Replicas. Cinny is stateless: two give a rolling update with no gap.

resources.description: Resources of the cinny container. A scheduling floor, not a sizing (VPA in `Off` mode gives recommendations). No CPU limit on purpose.

terminationGracePeriodSeconds.description: Seconds Cinny gets to stop (the server drains on SIGTERM).

topologySpreadConstraints.description: Topology spread constraints. Empty: the chart spreads the replicas over zones (`topology.kubernetes.io/zone`, `ScheduleAnyway`). A list you set replaces it and needs its own `labelSelector`.

enabled.description: Create a VerticalPodAutoscaler for Cinny (needs the VPA CRDs, see the `vertical-pod-autoscaler-crds` chart).

recommender.description: Recommender name (`spec.recommenders`, which takes at most one). Empty: the recommender named `default`.

config.description: tuwunel settings (the `[global]` table of `tuwunel.toml`, see `tuwunel-example.toml` upstream), rendered into a ConfigMap. Nested maps become `[global.<key>]` tables. Chart-owned keys (`server_name`, `database_path`, `address`, `port`, `unix_socket_path`) are rejected. With `ingress.wellKnown` or `httpRoute.wellKnown` the chart defaults `well_known.client` and `well_known.server`; your values win. Secrets go through `existingSecret` and the `*_file` options, never here.

options.description: DNS options (fewer search-list lookups for federation host names).

name.description: Name of a Secret to mount at `/etc/tuwunel/secrets` (mode 0440), for the `*_file` options: `registration_token_file`, `registration_shared_secret_file`, `turn_secret_file`, `ldap.bind_password_file`, `identity_provider[].client_secret_file`. Each key becomes a file. Empty: nothing mounted. The chart never creates it.

extraArgs.description: Extra `tuwunel` options, after the chart's own (none). Options for the config file and options that exit or start another mode are rejected.

extraEnv.description: Extra environment variables (`EnvVar` list) for the tuwunel container. `TUWUNEL_<KEY>` variables win over the config file. Variables for chart-owned settings and the config file path are rejected.

extraVolumeMounts.description: Extra volume mounts for the tuwunel container.

global.description: Global values are values that can be accessed from any chart or subchart by exactly the same name.

hostUsers.description: Run the pods in a user namespace (`false`: uid 65532 maps to an unprivileged host uid). Needs node support (containerd 2.0+ or CRI-O, runc 1.2+, kernel 6.3+) and idmapped mounts on every volume's file system (not NFS/SMB, not `hostPath` on some file systems); pods fail to start otherwise. `true` uses host users.

enabled.description: Create a Gateway API HTTPRoute for the homeserver (path prefix `/`).

hostnames.description: Host names (empty: any host of the Gateway listener). The first one is the homeserver host.

wellKnown.description: Delegate `serverName` to the homeserver host: create a second HTTPRoute (`<fullname>-well-known`) on host name `serverName`, path prefix `/.well-known/matrix`, and default `well_known.client` to `https://<first host name>` and `well_known.server` to `<first host name>:443`. Needs `hostnames`, and a Gateway listener accepting `serverName`.

digest.description: Image digest, only valid together with `image.tag`.

tag.description: Image tag. Empty: the tag and digest recorded for `image.repository` in the `artifacthub.io/images` annotation of `Chart.yaml`. When set, the chart digest is not applied; add `image.digest` to pin it.

enabled.description: Create an Ingress for the homeserver (path `/`).

hosts.description: Host names. Required when enabled. The first one is the homeserver host.

labels.description: Extra Ingress labels (for example the label an external-dns `--label-filter` selects).

wellKnown.description: Delegate `serverName` to the homeserver host: add a rule on host `serverName`, path `/.well-known/matrix`, and default `well_known.client` to `https://<first host>` and `well_known.server` to `<first host>:443`. For a `serverName` that differs from the homeserver host (`example.com` served by `matrix.example.com`). Needs `hosts`. Add `serverName` to `tls`.

livekit.description:
MatrixRTC calls: a LiveKit SFU and lk-jwt-service, which hands out LiveKit
tokens to Matrix users. Two Deployments of their own, apart from the homeserver.

config.description: LiveKit settings (`config.yaml`, see `config-sample.yaml` upstream), rendered into a ConfigMap. Chart-owned keys (`port`, `rtc.tcp_port`, `rtc.udp_port`, `key_file`, `prometheus.port`) are rejected. Keys go through `existingSecret`, never here. TURN, Redis and multi-node are out of scope.

enabled.description: Deploy LiveKit and lk-jwt-service (calls for Element Call and Element X). Needs `host` and `existingSecret.name`.

key.description: Key of the Secret: a file holding one line, `<api key>: <api secret>` (a secret of 32 characters or more).

name.description: Name of a Secret holding the LiveKit API key and secret, shared by LiveKit and lk-jwt-service. Required when enabled. The chart never creates it.

revision.description: Opaque string added to both pods as the `checksum/secret` annotation: change it when you rotate the Secret to restart them (a mounted Secret is not re-read by a running process). The chart cannot hash a Secret it does not own, so it is yours to set, for example from CI: `--set-string livekit.existingSecret.revision=$(kubectl get secret livekit-keys -o json | sha256sum | cut -c1-12)`. Empty: no annotation.

host.description: Public host of LiveKit and lk-jwt-service (one host for both, `calls.example.com`). Required when enabled. Clients get `https://<host>` from the homeserver (`well_known.livekit_url`), lk-jwt-service gets `wss://<host>`.

enabled.description: Create a Gateway API HTTPRoute on `livekit.host`: the lk-jwt-service paths go to lk-jwt-service, `/` to LiveKit (WebSocket).

digest.description: Image digest, only valid together with `livekit.image.tag`.

tag.description: Image tag. Empty: the tag and digest recorded for `livekit.image.repository` in the `artifacthub.io/images` annotation of `Chart.yaml`. When set, the chart digest is not applied; add `livekit.image.digest` to pin it.

enabled.description: Create an Ingress on `livekit.host`: the lk-jwt-service paths go to lk-jwt-service, `/` to LiveKit (WebSocket).

digest.description: Image digest, only valid together with `livekit.jwt.image.tag`.

tag.description: Image tag. Empty: the tag and digest recorded for `livekit.jwt.image.repository` in the `artifacthub.io/images` annotation of `Chart.yaml`. When set, the chart digest is not applied; add `livekit.jwt.image.digest` to pin it.

priorityClassName.description: Priority class name of the lk-jwt-service pod.

resources.description: Resources of the lk-jwt-service container. A scheduling floor, not a sizing.

terminationGracePeriodSeconds.description: Seconds lk-jwt-service gets to stop. It has no SIGTERM handler: a 5 s `preStop` sleep lets the endpoints drop the pod first, then the image's stop signal (SIGKILL) ends it.

enabled.description: Serve Prometheus metrics (`prometheus.port`, 6789) and name the container port `metrics`. On the node's address with `mode: hostNetwork`.
Create a Prometheus Operator PodMonitor (no Service needed). Exclusive with `serviceMonitor`.
Render the metrics Service (also rendered when `serviceMonitor.enabled`).
Create a Prometheus Operator ServiceMonitor. Exclusive with `podMonitor`.

nodeSelector.description: Node selector of the LiveKit pod, merged over `nodeSelector`. The host modes need the node with the public IP.

priorityClassName.description: Priority class name of the LiveKit pod.

resources.description: Resources of the livekit container. A scheduling floor, not a sizing. `GOMEMLIMIT` is 90% of `limits.memory` (an integer with a Ki/Mi/Gi/Ti or k/M/G/T suffix; any other form gets the full limit).

mode.description: How media (7881/tcp, 7882/udp, fixed) reaches the pod. `hostPort`: published on the node, which LiveKit advertises (`NODE_IP`, unless `config.rtc.node_ip` or `config.rtc.use_external_ip` is set). `hostNetwork`: the pod uses the node's network, LiveKit finds the addresses itself. `LoadBalancer`: a Service of its own, needs `config.rtc.node_ip` or `config.rtc.use_external_ip`. Both host modes need a namespace that allows privileged pods and a node with a public IP (`livekit.nodeSelector`).

annotations.description: Annotations of the media Service (`mode: LoadBalancer`).

externalTrafficPolicy.description: `externalTrafficPolicy` of the media Service. Empty: Kubernetes default.

loadBalancerClass.description: `loadBalancerClass` of the media Service. Empty: cloud provider default.

annotations.description: Annotations of the LiveKit Service (HTTP and WebSocket, 7880).

startupProbe.description: Startup probe (`GET /` on 7880, 406 until the node is ready).

terminationGracePeriodSeconds.description: Seconds LiveKit gets to stop: it drains on SIGTERM (no limit) and a second signal forces it. The longest call a rollout waits for.

nameOverride.description:
yaml-language-server: $schema=values.schema.json
Override the chart name used in resource names and labels.

from.description: NetworkPolicyPeer list allowed to reach the Cinny port. Empty: any source (browsers reach it through your ingress controller or gateway).

to.description: DNS peers (port 53 TCP/UDP). Override for NodeLocal DNSCache or non-standard labels.

enabled.description: Restrict egress (DNS, internet peers for federation, push and URL previews, `extraEgress`).

to.description: Internet peers (any port). Default: the internet, not the private, CGNAT and link-local ranges, so a compromised pod cannot move sideways. Remove an `except` entry to reach a server there.

enabled.description: Create a NetworkPolicy per component (ingress: the homeserver port).

from.description: NetworkPolicyPeer list allowed to reach the homeserver port. Empty: any source (clients, federation and the ingress controller can be anywhere).

NetworkPolicyPeer list allowed to reach LiveKit's HTTP and WebSocket port (7880). Empty: any source (clients through your ingress controller or gateway, lk-jwt-service). Media (7881/tcp, 7882/udp) is open to any source. Does not apply with `livekit.rtc.mode: hostNetwork`.
NetworkPolicyPeer list allowed to reach lk-jwt-service (8080). Empty: any source.
NetworkPolicyPeer list allowed to scrape LiveKit's metrics port (6789). Empty: any source.

nodeSelector.description: Node selector. With a `hostPath`, pin the pod to the node.

sizeLimit.description: Size limit (`type: emptyDir`, everything is lost with the pod). Empty: none.

name.description: Name of an existing PVC (`type: existingClaim`).

path.description: Absolute node path (`type: hostPath`), owned by uid/gid 65532. Pin the pod to the node.

type.description: `hostPath` type. `DirectoryOrCreate` makes a root-owned directory the server cannot write.
Where `/var/lib/tuwunel` (database and uploaded media) lives. `volumeClaimTemplate` creates a PVC and keeps it on uninstall; the other types use the matching sub-section.

size.description: Requested size. The database and every uploaded file live here: size it for media. The template is immutable once installed: resize the PVC, see the README.

podSecurityContext.description: Pod security context. Overrides are merged onto these defaults. `fsGroup` does not apply to NFS/SMB volumes or `hostPath`.

resources.description: Resources of the tuwunel container. A scheduling floor, not a sizing: memory grows with the number of rooms and the cache (measure, then tune; VPA in `Off` mode gives recommendations). No CPU limit on purpose.

securityContext.description: Container security context of the tuwunel container. Overrides are merged onto these defaults.

serverName.description: Matrix server name: the domain of user IDs (`

name.description: ServiceAccount name. Empty: `<fullname>` (or `default` when `create` is false).

startupProbe.description: Startup probe (`tuwunel --health-check`). 30 minutes: a start after an upgrade can run a long database migration, during which the listener is closed.

terminationGracePeriodSeconds.description: Seconds the homeserver gets to stop. Upstream asks for 1800: a start after an upgrade can run a one-way database migration, and a kill during it corrupts the database.

enabled.description: Create a VerticalPodAutoscaler for the homeserver (needs the VPA CRDs, see the `vertical-pod-autoscaler-crds` chart).

minAllowed.description: Lower bound of recommendations (for example `{cpu: 25m, memory: 64Mi}`).

recommender.description: Recommender name (`spec.recommenders`, which takes at most one). Empty: the recommender named `default`. Set it when the cluster's recommender runs under another `--recommender-name`: a VPA nobody serves gets no recommendation.
